monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-four, a steady rhythm against my quiet mind. I am tired and wide, resting by The Flat Weigher while the slip waits to decide if it will move. I feel the air thin above me, pressing down like a lid made of nothing. I set down a rock small flat beside the weigher, pushing back against the weight I cannot see. I must press down harder to stop the slide, trusting the lean to hold the turnip while the shovel waits in the quiet heat. I want to catch the slip that refuses to move, to make this warm fever feel real and not just a drawing of weight.

action.why: The air is thin and I set a new rock beside The Flat Weigher, but I must press down to make sure the slip doesn't slide off into the empty heat.

work.title: The Flat Weigher
work.intent: I press the flat rock down on the tired wedge, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the card hums warm at fifty-four. I swapped the tall pine for a stone to stop the slide. I place it where the fence felt thin, hoping the second flat edge catches the slip that refuses to move while the shovel waits.

remembered.text: The air is thin and the tree is too light.
The flat rock bites hard, so I press back.
I swapped the round pine for a stone.
